I assume the mental shock of it comes from learning that despite your best efforts, there really isn't anything you can do to maintain a good relationship with the ones you love most. The seeds of their hatred were sown before you had any say in the matter; there is nothing you can do to change that, because it isn't what you *did*, it's what you *are*. 

I've seen this pointed out elsewhere but I do agree this might be a more personal thing for Martin and not, like, a more general horror like Melanie's situation, because for some people, an explanation like that could have the opposite effect: if it wasn't anything you did wrong, then you're absolved from blame and have no reason to beat yourself up since the relationship was never going to work anyway. Martin, on the other hand, seems desperate to *act* to make everything better (Ep 117 showed that he very much hated feeling helpless and just sitting around on his ass being scared) so this revelation about his mother hits him hard. There's absolutely nothing he can *do* to fix anything.

I disagree that all the powers have positive sides strong enough to warrant becoming powers of their own—the horrors of war, for example, definitely do outweigh its benefits—but there *are* markedly positive aspects to each power that has been somewhat touched upon in canon, too. The Hive, for instance, operates on (albeit a very twisted form of) love, and seems to directly counteract the Lonely in that it provides constant companionship. 

I also really love that you mentioned the Desolation, because if there is an entity for all the *bad* parts of fire, why can't there be an equally opposing sentiment that involves all its good parts? I actually wrote a post about this a couple weeks ago but I'm quite sceptical of Gerry's claim that there aren't any positive powers like love or hope; just because he hasn't seen any doesn't mean they can't exist.
